editorial.headline: Sheet Glass Wholesale: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, sheet-glass wholesale is nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the province’s permanent risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this sheet-glass wholesale activity as PMA in Bali today, even though the national PMA position is open. The activity is defined around wholesale trade in construction sheet glass: clear sheets, opaque sheets, coloured clear sheets, and engraved sheets. It is a commercial category for those stated forms of flat glass, with construction material as the use context supplied by the record. That specificity matters: the scope identifies the sheet formats and finishes that make up this activity’s stated subject matter.

Registration is open across the full scale range named in the record: Micro, Small, Medium, and Large. Nationally, foreign ownership may reach 100%. The open PMA status therefore carries a full foreign-ownership ceiling. For a founder considering whether the national setting permits foreign capital, the answer from this record is direct: it does. The cited PMA references are Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021, and the record gives no narrower national ownership cap for this activity.

Bali changes the practical answer decisively. The record marks the activity as blocked for PMA registration under the province’s risk-class moratorium. At the Large scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope. Bali’s stated rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration, island-wide and permanently. The record identifies the moratorium as applying from May 2026. On the information supplied, that is why the otherwise open national position cannot be used to register this activity as PMA in Bali.

The distinction should not be softened away. The 100% figure is the national ceiling; it is not a Bali registration approval. The listed enterprise scales show that the activity is open across those scales, while the Bali rule operates through the risk classification specified for Large scale. No separate Bali-side foreign-ownership percentage is stated here, because the record’s Bali outcome is a block rather than a local cap. For a Bali project, the operative conclusion is simple: PMA registration is unavailable today.
editorial.pullQuote: A national ceiling of 100% is not a Bali registration approval.
